title: Aegon Stride Quickstart credits and routing discovery
summary: Discovery call to qualify Aegon Stride's needs for a quick self-serve onramp using Redwood API. Discussed credit allocation, TTFT goals, routing policies between hosted/dedicated/private, security requirements (SSO, KMS, SOC 2), and next steps for a two-week pilot and technical deep dive.
next_steps: Olivia to send pricing + pilot agreement and example SLOs
Marcus to schedule technical deep dive / performance benchmark session (SE-led)
Customer to share sample prompt set and success metrics
Leah to open trial account and allocate quickstart credits
action_items: Olivia Chen: Send pilot pricing sheet, quickstart runbook, and security FAQ (due 2026-05-12)
Marcus Patel: Schedule and prepare benchmark deck + perf checklist (due 2026-05-11)
Sofia Alvarez: Share top 20 prompt examples and expected token volumes (due 2026-05-10)
Leah Torres: Create trial tenant and provision credits (due 2026-05-08)
Tom Bowers: Provide network details for VPC peering discussion (due 2026-05-13)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-07 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC — Duration: 46m. Attendees listed in metadata.

[00:00] Olivia Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Olivia from Redwood, AE on this region—uh—happy to kick off. Marcus, Leah — wanna do quick intros?
[00:08] Marcus Patel: Hey all, Marcus, solutions engineer. I'll handle the deeper perf and deployment stuff.
[00:11] Leah Torres: Leah, CSM — I'll make sure the pilot runbook and credits line up.
[00:15] Sofia Alvarez: Hi, I'm Sofia, CTO at Aegon Stride. We've got Rajesh, Emily, Tom on the line. Quick note: we're evaluating options to put an LLM layer in our customer support stack, need to know TTFT and privacy.
[00:29] Rajesh Malhotra: Yeah hi. Main constraints: sub-100ms token latency for short replies, and data residency in EU for PII snippets.
[00:36] Emily Park: Product is running a beta, timeline is 6–8 weeks to rollout. Looking for quick way to test without heavy infra lift.
[00:44] Tom Bowers: I'm infra — interested in VPC and key management details.

[00:50] Olivia Chen: Great. High-level: Redwood offers hosted API for fastest TTFT, Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data. For a quickstart pilot we usually recommend hosted with quickstart credits so you get to first token in hours.
[01:05] Sofia Alvarez: When you say 'hours'—what are we realistically talking about?
[01:09] Olivia Chen: If you self-serve and we provision credits, you can get an API key and make calls in under two hours; if you want SSO + VPC private connectivity, that'll add more setup — usually a few days to a couple weeks depending on firewall rules.
[01:23] Rajesh Malhotra: Two hours sounds promising. But latency—how do you hit sub-100ms? Is that with hosted?
[01:30] Marcus Patel: So latency depends on model choice and sequence length. For small chat responses we recommend a compact open model variant. On hosted, we've got regioned endpoints and optimized kernels; real-world median per-token latencies for 128-token responses land in the low hundreds, but small payloads can be under 100ms with the right model and batching off. If you need strict p99 under 100ms we usually suggest Dedicated or a routing policy to a lower-latency zone.
[01:54] Emily Park: Ok so possibly start hosted for speed and move to dedicated when we need more consistency. Is that a common path?
[01:59] Olivia Chen: Very common PLG path — hosted quickstart, then Dedicated reservation as you scale. You can pin model versions and keep call signatures the same so switching is seamless.

[02:12] Tom Bowers: Question on data: we send user messages that sometimes include PII. How long do you retain logs? Can we turn off retention?
[02:20] Leah Torres: We have options. For hosted, standard retention is configurable and we offer data deletion and no-retention tiers on enterprise plans. For Private, logs stay in your environment. We also support KMS integrations for envelope encryption.
[02:32] Sofia Alvarez: Do you have SOC 2 and customer audit reports?
[02:36] Olivia Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, plus ISO in progress. We'll send the security pack. I'll attach SOC 2 and our data handling FAQ.

[02:45] Rajesh Malhotra: For the quickstart pilot are there limits on throughput? We expect spikes during the beta.
[02:51] Marcus Patel: Quickstart credits are typically throttled to protect shared capacity; we can set a burst limit and guidance for request shaping. If you expect consistent high throughput, Dedicated capacity is best — predictable throughput and autoscaling rules. For the pilot we can provision a modest burst profile.
[03:06] Sofia Alvarez: Can you do region preference—EU only?
[03:09] Olivia Chen: Yes we can restrict routing to EU regions for hosted; for Private you'd deploy to your EU VPC.

[03:16] Emily Park: Walk us through steps to get to first token if we take quickstart credits today.
[03:20] Leah Torres: Step 1: we open a trial tenant, allocate credits. Step 2: you get API keys and SDK examples; Step 3: you run a small smoke test and we assist with a perf checklist. We can do a guided session and Marcus can run a live test to measure latency.
[03:34] Rajesh Malhotra: For the smoke test can you emulate our prompt patterns? We use multi-turn summaries and reranking for suggestions.
[03:41] Marcus Patel: Yes — please share your top 20 prompts, typical lengths and token expectations. We can run them against the model variants. We'll also test KV cache behavior — note sometimes transcripts show 'K V cash' in auto-gen but it's KV cache.
[03:54] Sofia Alvarez: Haha noted.

[04:00] Olivia Chen: A couple tradeoffs to call out: batching reduces cost but increases latency; prefix or KV caching improves cost and latency for repeated context but requires planning for cache warmup. Also quantized model variants lower cost at some quality tradeoff.
[04:18] Emily Park: Any admin UI or console for observing token costs per route?
[04:21] Leah Torres: Redwood Console has token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, tracing hooks. We'll show you the console in the next demo.
[04:30] Tom Bowers: About SSO — we use Okta and need SCIM + SAML.
[04:35] Olivia Chen: Okta SAML is supported; SCIM for provisioning on enterprise plans. We'll include the SSO integration guide.

[04:43] Rajesh Malhotra: Is model versioning supported? If a new model causes regressions can we roll back?
[04:48] Marcus Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions and set rollout rules. We also support canary and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. Redwood Optimize can surface quality regressions against prompt sets.

[05:00] Sofia Alvarez: Pricing — can you give ballpark for usage on hosted during pilot? We're trying to estimate credits.
[05:06] Olivia Chen: For a two-week pilot, typical spend for teams doing smoke tests and small scale UI integration is 2k–10k credits depending on call volume and model. We'll send a pilot template that maps expected tokens to credit burn.
[05:17] Emily Park: Great. We want to measure TTFT (time-to-first-token) after a cold start and p95 latency under typical load. Can you run those with the pilot?
[05:26] Marcus Patel: Yes. We'll include cold-start and p95 tests in the perf checklist and record traces. We can also run a short A/B between compact and standard variants.

[05:36] Tom Bowers: On network side, if we later go Private and want VPC peering, what info do you need?
[05:41] Olivia Chen: We'll need CIDR ranges, firewall rules, and whether you want direct peering or VPN. For on-prem we'll need outbound/inbound details. Tom, if you can send those after the call we'll loop in infra engineering.
[05:54] Sofia Alvarez: Any gotchas when moving from hosted to Dedicated?
[05:57] Marcus Patel: Mostly capacity planning — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and consistent SLOs. There's a contract and lead time for capacity provisioning. Also, routing policies and canary rollouts are smoother once you have a pinned model.
[06:10] Rajesh Malhotra: For the demo/perf run what does Redwood need from us?
[06:14] Leah Torres: Prompt set, traffic profile (qps), expected p95 target and any security constraints. Also confirm which region.
[06:23] Emily Park: We'll share prompt set and target of p95 < 200ms initially for beta.
[06:29] Sofia Alvarez: Timeline — we want to start pilot next week if possible.
[06:33] Olivia Chen: That's doable. Leah will provision credits immediately after this call, and Olivia will send the pilot agreement. Marcus will follow up to book the perf session within three business days.

[06:45] Rajesh Malhotra: One more question — do you support hardware affinitization for Dedicated? We use A100s for heavy long-form batch jobs; for inference we'd likely use lower mem GPUs.
[06:56] Marcus Patel: Yes, Dedicated can be configured with GPU families. We recommend matching model footprint to instance type; we can propose quantized variants to fit cheaper GPUs for low-latency inference.
[07:08] Tom Bowers: About billing — is pilot usage billed post-credit? How do we track?
[07:13] Leah Torres: Pilot consumption draws from allocated credits. We'll provide a ledger in the console. After credits are exhausted we'd switch to pay-as-you-go or sign a reserved capacity agreement.
[07:24] Emily Park: Any reference customers with EU privacy constraints?
[07:28] Olivia Chen: Yes — we've worked with a few fintechs and healthtech teams; I'll include two redacted case studies focusing on EU-only deployments and KMS.

[07:36] Sofia Alvarez: Sounds good. Quick question — does Redwood offer any prebuilt connectors for Zendesk?
[07:42] Marcus Patel: We have community SDKs and a Zendesk reference integration as a starting point. We can share the repo.

[07:49] Olivia Chen: Let's recap action items and next steps.
[07:52] Olivia Chen: Olivia — I'll send pricing, SOC 2, SSO guide, pilot agreement and the quickstart runbook. Marcus — you'll schedule the perf deep dive and prepare bench deck. Leah — create tenant and top up credits. Customer — Sofia/Rajesh/Emily to share prompt set and qps estimates; Tom to share network info if we need VPC details.
[08:16] Rajesh Malhotra: Agreed. Any blockers?
[08:19] Sofia Alvarez: None from product; just need internal signoff on quick pilot.
[08:23] Tom Bowers: I'll get the network info.
[08:26] Emily Park: We'll try to turn around prompts today or tomorrow.
[08:30] Olivia Chen: Great — we'll follow up with calendar holds. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] End of call.
